steps.name: partial_draft
steps.text:
Sales forecasting is one of the earliest forecasting applications and one of the most demanded ones. For economic and financial reasons, being able to anticipate what customers need and how they behave can make a big difference for commercial activity, especially when large volumes of goods have to be managed. The forecasting of time series with a known historical past has been analysed a lot, but very little attention has been given to a scenario that is much more practical and challenging, which is forecasting new products that the market has not seen before. In many cases these forecasts are made in a judgmental way by experts, who basically take into account the characteristics of the newly designed product together with information on what is trending in the market right now, and make an educated guess.

In this paper we propose a non-autoregressive Transformer model called GTM-Transformer, which tries to mimic this behavior. It models the sales of new products based on information from several domains (modalities): the product image; textual descriptors of category, color and fabric; temporal information in the planned release date; and exogenous information on the trending tendencies of the textual descriptors, in the form of Google Trends. This last component is a crucial part of GTM-Transformer, because it brings external information on item popularity into the reasoning. Intuitively it models what people are interested in, and it turns out to be important for the forecasting performance.

- Google Trends
  - predict diverse time series (real estate sales to inflation expectations)
  - clothing sales: only suggested in one previous work, never tried in practice, esp. new products
  - valuable when encoded appropriately
  - Cross-Attention weights: most useful info around end of previous year's same fashion season, seven to ten months before exposure
- VISUELLE
  - first public dataset for new fashion product sales forecasting
  - real fast fashion company Nunalie; 5577 new products, about 45M sales, 2016-2019 seasons
  - image, textual metadata, sales after first release date, three Google Trends (category, color, fabric)
  - compare with few recent state-of-the-art alternatives: best on several metrics
  - attributes inferred from image (Fashion IQ) improve performance
- Organization: next Sec. literature; Sec. 3 VISUELLE; Sec. 4 GTM-Transformer; Sec. 5 experiments; Sec. 6 conclusions

steps.name: rough_draft
steps.text:
Sales forecasting is one of the earliest forecasting applications and one of the most demanded ones. For economic and financial reasons, being able to anticipate what customers need and how they behave can make a big difference for commercial activity, especially when large volumes of goods have to be managed. The forecasting of time series with a known historical past has been analysed a lot, but very little attention has been given to a scenario that is much more practical and challenging, which is forecasting new products that the market has not seen before. In many cases these forecasts are made in a judgmental way by experts, who basically take into account the characteristics of the newly designed product together with information on what is trending in the market right now, and make an educated guess.

In this paper we propose a non-autoregressive Transformer model called GTM-Transformer, which tries to mimic this behavior. It models the sales of new products based on information from several domains (modalities): the product image; textual descriptors of category, color and fabric; temporal information in the planned release date; and exogenous information on the trending tendencies of the textual descriptors, in the form of Google Trends. This last component is a crucial part of GTM-Transformer, because it brings external information on item popularity into the reasoning. Intuitively it models what people are interested in, and it turns out to be important for the forecasting performance.

It has already been shown that Google Trends can be used to predict diverse types of time series (from real estate sales to inflation expectations), but using them for clothing sales forecasting has only been suggested in one previous work and never tried in practice, especially in a new product forecasting setting. On the technical side, we show that Google Trends are valuable when they are encoded appropriately. Using the Cross-Attention weights of our model, we find that the most useful information is systematically located around the end of the same fashion season of the previous year, i.e., seven to ten months before the product is planned for exposure.

Our second contribution is VISUELLE, the first public dataset for new fashion product sales forecasting. VISUELLE is a repository built on the data of a real fast fashion company, Nunalie, and it is composed of 5577 new products and about 45M sales related to the fashion seasons from 2016-2019. Every product in VISUELLE comes with multimodal information: an image, textual metadata, the sales after the first release date, and three related Google Trends that describe the popularity of category, color and fabric. We use VISUELLE to compare GTM-Transformer with the few recent state-of-the-art alternatives in the literature on new product sales forecasting, and we get the best performance on several forecasting metrics. We also show that the model can be enriched with attributes that are inferred automatically from the image, using the widely-used Fashion IQ attributes, which improves the final performance.

The rest of the paper is organized like this: the next Sec. gives a general overview of the literature on forecasting in fashion and on new product sales forecasting. Sec. 3 gives an overview of the VISUELLE dataset, showing what information is available and how the dataset can be used for further research on this topic. Sec. 4 explains the methodological background and the details of GTM-Transformer. Sec. 5 explains the experiments thoroughly and finally Sec. 6 draws the conclusions.

steps.name: revised_draft
steps.text:
Sales forecasting is one of the earliest and most demanded forecasting applications [1,2]. Driven by economic and financial reasons, the ability to anticipate the needs and behavior of customers can make a big difference for commercial activity, especially when large volumes of goods have to be managed. While the forecasting of time series with a known historical past has been analysed extensively [3,4], very little attention has been paid to a much more practical and challenging scenario: forecasting new products, which the market has not seen before. In many cases, such forecasts are made in a judgmental manner [3] by experts who essentially consider the characteristics of the newly designed product together with information on what is currently trending in the market to make an educated guess.

In this paper, we propose a non-autoregressive Transformer [5] model dubbed GTM-Transformer, which tries to mimic this behavior by modeling the sales of new products based on information coming from several domains (modalities): the product image; textual descriptors of category, color and fabric; temporal information in the planned release date; and exogenous information on the trending tendencies of the textual descriptors, in the form of Google Trends. This last component is a crucial part of GTM-Transformer, since it brings external information on item popularity into the reasoning. Intuitively, it models what people are interested in, and it proves important for forecasting performance.

While it has already been shown that Google Trends can be used to predict diverse types of time series (from real estate sales to inflation expectations) [6,7,8,9,10,11], their adoption for clothing sales forecasting has only been suggested in [12] and never tried in practice, especially in a new product forecasting setting. Technically, we demonstrate that Google Trends are valuable when encoded appropriately. Thanks to the Cross-Attention weights of our model, we find that the most useful information is systematically located around the end of the previous year's same fashion season, i.e., seven to ten months before the product is planned for exposure.

As a second contribution, we present VISUELLE: the first public dataset for new fashion product sales forecasting. VISUELLE is a repository built upon the data of a real fast fashion company, Nunalie, and is composed of 5577 new products and about 45M sales related to fashion seasons from 2016-2019. Each product in VISUELLE comes with multimodal information: an image, textual metadata, sales after the first release date, and three related Google Trends describing category, color and fabric popularity. We use VISUELLE to compare GTM-Transformer with the few recent state-of-the-art alternatives in the new product sales forecasting literature, obtaining the best performance on several forecasting metrics. We also show that the model can be enriched with attributes automatically inferred from the image, using the widely-used Fashion IQ attributes [13], which improves the final performance.

The rest of the paper is organized as follows: the next Sec. provides a general overview of the literature on forecasting in fashion and new product sales forecasting. In Sec. 3, an overview of the VISUELLE dataset is given, showing the available information and how the dataset can be used for further research on this topic. Sec. 4 explains the methodological background and details of GTM-Transformer. In Sec. 5 the experiments are thoroughly explained, and finally conclusions are drawn in Sec. 6.
